newsitem.title: USA: COWBOYS' IRVIN AND WILLIAMS SUSPECTS IN RAPE CASE.
newsitem.headline: COWBOYS' IRVIN AND WILLIAMS SUSPECTS IN RAPE CASE.

text.p: Dallas Cowboys superstars Michael Irvin and Erik Williams are under investigation for allegedly sexually assaulting a woman who said she was raped at gunpoint at Williams' home, police said on Tuesday.
Dallas police Lieutenant David Goelden said no arrest warrants had yet been filed against Irvin or Williams but that the two Pro-Bowl stars and another man were being investigated.
The 23-year-old woman told police that Irvin placed a gun against her head while Williams and the other man raped her at William's home on Sunday night. The suspects allegedly videotaped the assault.

"She was visiting and apparently things got out of hand and she was forced to have sex with these two individuals against her will," Goelden told a news conference. "If there is sufficent evidence to file charges, we will file charges."
Police searched Williams' home on Tuesday and took away possible physical evidence, including a videotape.

It was the latest in a string of scandals to rock the Cowboys team, which has won the Super Bowl three of the last four years and was preparing for a second round playoff game against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte, N.C., on Sunday.
Irvin, a 30-year-old wide receiver, earlier this year pleaded no contest to felony cocaine possession charges after police found him and a former Cowboys player in a motel room with two strippers.

He was sentenced to four years deferred adjudication, fined $10,000 and ordered to do 800 hours of community service. The National Football League then suspended Irvin for the first five games of the 1996-1997 season.
State District Judge Manny Alvarez also warned Irvin he would sentence him to up to 20 years in prison if he got into further trouble.
Williams, a 28-year-old offensive tackle, was in 1995 accused of sexually assaulting a 17-year-old topless dancer but a grand jury declined to indict him, saying there was insufficent evidence.
Both Irvin and Williams were key players in the Cowboys' run of Super Bowl victories in the 1990s.

A spokesman for the Dallas Cowboys said the team's management would hold a news conference later on Tuesday. Irvin and Williams were on the practice field preparing for Sunday's game when the assault allegations were detailed by police.
The allegations were certain to bring fresh condemnation of the Dallas Cowboys, which was once known as "America's Team" but has been besieged by scandal in the last two years.
Even some die-hard fans are beginning to turn against the team, sickened by sordid tales of drug use, abuse against women and of players cavorting with prostitutes.
In November, star defensive lineman Leon Lett was suspended by the NFL for a year after failing a drug test.
